ext_description.message: Search from the address bar or drag text to the tab strip to compare two search engines side by side in Chrome’s split view.
ext_description.description: Extension description shown in the Chrome Web Store and chrome://extensions.

ext_action_title.description: Tooltip of the toolbar button, which opens the Split Search popup. Keep the product name Split Search untranslated.

go_status_opening.description: Status line on the trigger page while the split view is being opened (shown only for a moment).

go_status_failed.description: Status line on the trigger page when the split view could not be opened; an error box with the reason follows.

go_status_kept.message: The results are open in a new split view to the right. You can close this tab.
go_status_kept.description: Status line on the trigger page after the results were opened in a new split view next to the current one and this tab could not close itself; tells the user they may close the page.

go_status_no_repeat.message: This page won’t open the split view again on its own.
go_status_no_repeat.description: Status line when the user comes back to the trigger page via Back, Forward or reload: the page does not open the split view again by itself (a Run again button is offered).

go_btn_rerun.description: Button on the trigger page that runs the split search again after Back/Forward/reload.

go_btn_left_only.message: Search with the left engine only
go_btn_left_only.description: Button on the trigger page error screen: open only the left engine's search (a normal search, no split view).

go_err_no_trigger.message: This page didn’t receive a trigger URL. Search from the address bar or drag text onto the tab strip instead of opening this page directly.
go_err_no_trigger.description: Error on the trigger page when it was opened without a trigger URL (e.g. typed directly); the user should start a search from the address bar or by drag-and-drop instead.

go_err_config_unreadable.message: The settings couldn’t be read and the trigger URL isn’t recognized, so there’s no search to open. Turn Split Search off and on again on the Extensions page (chrome://extensions), or restart Chrome, then search again.
go_err_config_unreadable.description: Error on the trigger page: the settings could not be read and the trigger URL is not a usable http(s) URL, so not even the left search can be opened.

go_err_bad_template.message: The URL template for $ENGINE$ is invalid, so it can’t be the left engine. Check its URL on the settings page.
go_err_bad_template.description: Error on the trigger page: the left engine's URL template is invalid; the user should check it on the settings page. The placeholder is the engine name (not translated).

go_err_bad_url.message: The trigger URL isn’t recognized. It may have been cut off or changed. Search again, or copy a fresh trigger URL from the settings page.
go_err_bad_url.description: Error on the trigger page: the trigger URL cannot be parsed; the user should search again or copy the trigger URL again from the settings page.

go_err_not_left.message: $ENGINE$’s URL can’t be used on the left. Check its URL on the settings page, or pick a different left engine.
go_err_not_left.description: Error on the trigger page: the left engine's URL template cannot be used as the left side of a split view. The placeholder is the engine name (not translated).

engine_tpl_ok.message: Can be used on the left or right
engine_tpl_ok.description: Live hint under the URL template field in the engine dialog: the template can be used on either side of the split view.

engine_tpl_right_only.message: Right side only. A URL on the left needs a lowercase %s exactly once, as the whole value of a query parameter (e.g. ?q=%s). That parameter name can appear only once, and the URL can’t contain #.
engine_tpl_right_only.description: Live hint under the URL template field: the template can only be used on the right side. Contains the full 'can be left side' rule; keep the rule wording identical to err_default_left_url. Do not translate %s, ?q=%s or #.

err_bad_url.description: Error: the URL (template or trigger URL) cannot be parsed.

err_tpl_no_placeholder.message: The URL must contain a lowercase %s
err_tpl_no_placeholder.description: Error in the URL template field: the template lacks the lowercase %s placeholder. Do not translate %s.

err_tpl_bad_scheme.message: The URL must start with http:// or https://
err_tpl_bad_scheme.description: Error in the URL template field: the template does not use http or https.

err_tpl_no_host.description: Error in the URL template field: the template has no host name.

err_tpl_wildcard_host.message: The domain can’t contain *. Enter the site’s actual address.
err_tpl_wildcard_host.description: Error in the URL template field: the host name contains a * wildcard.

err_tpl_ipv6.message: IPv6 addresses aren’t supported. Use a domain name instead.
err_tpl_ipv6.description: Error in the URL template field: the host is an IPv6 address literal.

err_tpl_reserved_param.message: The URL can’t contain _ss. It’s a reserved parameter.
err_tpl_reserved_param.description: Error in the URL template field: the template contains the reserved _ss parameter. Do not translate _ss.

err_marker_format.message: The trigger URL is incomplete or malformed. Copy it again from the settings page.
err_marker_format.description: Error page after a search: the trigger URL is incomplete or malformed (its engine marker is not two engine ids). Don't mention the parameter name; tell the user to copy the trigger URL again.

err_unknown_engine.message: Split Search can’t find the engine “$ENGINE_ID$” that this site search points to. It may have been deleted or hidden, or the site search’s URL may have been edited. Delete or fix the site search in Chrome’s search engine settings, or add the engine again on the settings page.
err_unknown_engine.description: Error page after a search: the trigger URL names an engine id that does not exist (the engine was deleted or hidden, or the site search URL was edited).

err_not_left.message: $ENGINE$ can’t be used as the left engine
err_not_left.description: Error: the named engine's URL template cannot be used as the left side of a split view.

err_template_mismatch.message: The trigger URL doesn’t match the left engine’s current URL template, possibly because the engine’s URL was edited. Copy the trigger URL again from the settings page and update the site search with it.
err_template_mismatch.description: Error page after a search: the trigger URL no longer matches the left engine's current template; the user must copy the trigger URL again from the settings page.

err_config_too_large.description: Error when saving settings: one stored item exceeds chrome.storage.sync's per-item size limit. The placeholder is an internal storage key name (not translated).

err_name_required.description: Error in the engine dialog: the name field is empty.

err_name_too_long.message: The name can’t be longer than $MAX$ characters
err_name_too_long.description: Error in the engine dialog: the name is longer than the maximum number of characters.

err_id_format.message: The ID must be 1 to 20 characters: lowercase letters, digits or -
err_id_format.description: Error in the engine dialog: the engine id has invalid characters or length.

err_id_taken.message: The ID “$ID$” is already taken. Choose another one.
err_id_taken.description: Error in the engine dialog: another engine already uses this id.

err_id_exhausted.message: The ID “$ID$” and $ID$-2 through $ID$-99 are all taken. Delete some engines, then try again.
err_id_exhausted.description: Error when adding from the engine catalog: the catalog id and every numbered variant (id-2 … id-99) are already used by other engines.

err_engine_gone.message: This engine no longer exists. It may have been deleted on another device.
err_engine_gone.description: Error in the engine dialog: the engine being edited no longer exists (probably deleted on another synced device).

err_default_left_url.message: Can’t save: this engine is on the left of the default pair, and the new URL can’t be used on the left. A URL on the left needs a lowercase %s exactly once, as the whole value of a query parameter (e.g. ?q=%s). That parameter name can appear only once, and the URL can’t contain #. To use this URL anyway, first put a different engine on the left of the default pair.
err_default_left_url.description: Error in the engine dialog: the engine is the left side of the default pair and the new URL cannot be a left side. Contains the full 'can be left side' rule; keep the rule wording identical to engine_tpl_right_only. Do not translate %s, ?q=%s or #.

err_only_preset_hide.message: Only built-in engines can be hidden
err_only_preset_hide.description: Error: only preset engines can be hidden.

err_pair_uses_hide.message: The default pair uses this engine, so it can’t be hidden
err_pair_uses_hide.description: Error: the engine cannot be hidden because the default pair uses it.

err_only_custom_delete.message: Only custom engines can be deleted
err_only_custom_delete.description: Error: only custom engines can be deleted.

err_pair_uses_delete.message: The default pair uses this engine, so it can’t be deleted
err_pair_uses_delete.description: Error: the engine cannot be deleted because the default pair uses it.

err_pair_missing.message: A selected engine no longer exists. It may have been deleted or hidden.
err_pair_missing.description: Error when setting the default pair: a selected engine no longer exists (deleted or hidden).

err_quota_rate.message: You’re saving too often. Try again in a moment.
err_quota_rate.description: Error when saving settings: chrome.storage.sync write rate limit reached.

err_quota_bytes.message: Sync storage is full. Delete some custom engines or shorten names and URLs, then try again.
err_quota_bytes.description: Error when saving settings: chrome.storage.sync total storage quota is full.

options_title.description: Settings page title: browser tab title and the page heading. Keep the product name Split Search untranslated.

options_tagline.message: Search from the address bar, or drag text to the tab strip, and get results from two search engines at once in Chrome’s split view.
options_tagline.description: One-line summary under the settings page heading.

options_tabs_label.description: Accessible name (aria-label) of the tab list at the top of the settings page; not shown on screen.

options_tab_add.description: Name of the settings tab that explains how to add the trigger URL to Chrome; same wording as the card heading options_guide_title.

options_tab_pair.description: Name of the settings tab with the default pair (left and right search engines) and the keyword rules.

options_tab_engines.description: Name of the settings tab with the search engine list and the keyboard shortcut; use Chrome's term for search engines.

options_tab_lookup.description: Name of the settings tab for right-click lookup (selected text and image search).

options_tab_todo.description: Screen-reader-only text appended to the name of the "Add to Chrome" tab while setup is not finished; not shown on screen (a dot is shown instead).

options_tab_regrant.description: Screen-reader-only text appended to the name of the "Add to Chrome" tab when the left engine has lost its access; not shown on screen (a warning icon is shown instead).

options_pair_title.description: Heading of the settings card where the user picks the default engine pair (left and right engine).

options_pair_hint.message: Searching from the address bar or dragging text to the tab strip opens these two engines in a split view.
options_pair_hint.description: Hint under the default pair card heading: what the default pair is used for. Split view is Chrome's feature name; keep the Chrome term.

options_pair_other.message: Want more pairs? Create their trigger URLs in “$LINK$”.
options_pair_other.description: Last line of the default pair card. $LINK$ is a link whose text is the tab name options_tab_add; it opens that tab and expands “Other pairs”.

options_pair_chrome_hint.message: Chrome’s default search is set separately. After changing this pair, update its site search URL in Chrome and make sure it is the default. $STEPS$
options_pair_chrome_hint.description: Persistent neutral reminder below the default pair selectors. Chrome’s default search is configured separately; changing the pair requires updating the matching site search URL and checking that it is the default. This is guidance, not detected status. $STEPS$ is the link to the setup steps.

options_pair_changed.message: Your default pair is now $PAIR$. Copy the URL below, update the matching site search in Chrome, and make sure it is the default.
options_pair_changed.description: Box shown after changing the default pair on this page once setup is done: asks the user to update the matching site search in Chrome and check that it is the default. Does not claim to have read Chrome’s settings. $PAIR$ is the new pair, such as “Google | Bing”.

options_pair_changed_setup.message: The URL in “Get started” now uses the new pair.
options_pair_changed_setup.description: Box shown in the default pair card after the pair was changed during first-run setup. The quoted card name must match setup_title.

options_pair_changed_steps.description: Link below the default pair selectors or in the changed-pair box; opens the setup steps in the Add to Chrome tab.

options_pair_changed_continue.description: Link in the changed-pair box during first-run setup; goes back to the “Get started” card.

options_guide_title.description: Heading of the settings card that explains how to add the trigger URL to Chrome as a site search.

guide_steps_title.description: Subheading above the numbered setup steps.

guide_step_open_settings.message: Open Chrome’s search engine settings. Web pages can’t open this address directly, so copy it and paste it into the address bar:
guide_step_open_settings.description: Setup step 1. The address chrome://settings/searchEngines and a Copy button follow right after this sentence, so it ends with a colon.

guide_copy_settings_url.description: Button next to chrome://settings/searchEngines (setup guide and Get started step 2): copies that address.

guide_copy_default_aria.message: Copy the default pair’s trigger URL
guide_copy_default_aria.description: Accessible name of the Copy button next to the default pair's trigger URL. Must start with the visible Copy text (common_copy).

guide_copy_gen_aria.message: Copy the selected pair’s trigger URL
guide_copy_gen_aria.description: Accessible name of the Copy button next to the trigger URL of the pair picked under “Other pairs”. Must start with the visible Copy text (common_copy).

guide_copy_settings_aria.message: Copy address: Chrome search engine settings
guide_copy_settings_aria.description: Accessible name of the button that copies chrome://settings/searchEngines. Must start with the visible text (guide_copy_settings_url).

guide_step_add.description: Setup step 2. "Site search" and "Add" must match Chrome's own labels on chrome://settings/searchEngines in this language.

guide_step_fields.message: Enter any name (e.g. “Google | Bing”) and a shortcut of your choice (e.g. $KEYWORD$). In “URL with %s in place of query”, paste the trigger URL of the pair you want to use. Then click “Add”.
guide_step_fields.description: Setup step 3: what to type into Chrome's site search dialog. "Shortcut" must match Chrome's label. The placeholder becomes the example shortcut (guide_example_keyword) shown as code.

guide_example_keyword.description: Example site search shortcut for a Google | Bing pair, shown as code in setup step 3. Pick a short, natural shortcut for this language; ASCII letters only.

guide_step_default.message: For the default pair, open the ⋮ menu next to the new entry and choose “Make default”. Other pairs don’t need to be the default. To use one, type “shortcut + space + search terms” in the address bar.
guide_step_default.description: Setup step 4. "Make default" and "shortcut" must match Chrome's labels; ⋮ is the More actions menu icon.

guide_step_grant.message: In “$LINK$”, make sure the left engine shows “Access granted”.
guide_step_grant.description: Setup step 5. $LINK$ is a link whose text is the tab name options_tab_engines. The quoted status must match engine_granted.

guide_caveats_title.description: Subheading above the list of caveats.

guide_caveat_degrade.message: In these cases the trigger URL runs a normal search on the left engine and no split view opens: on other computers and phones that sync these search settings, in Incognito windows, when the extension is disabled or its access is revoked, and when the left engine’s site handles its own page loads (Perplexity, for example).
guide_caveat_degrade.description: Caveat: cases where the trigger URL falls back to a plain search with the left engine. The last case is a site that handles its own page loads (technically, its service worker takes over navigation); say it in plain words, without mentioning service workers.

guide_caveat_no_suggest.message: Site searches you add yourself have no suggestion URL, so while one is your default, the address bar shows no search suggestions.
guide_caveat_no_suggest.description: Caveat: a user-added site search has no suggestion URL, so the address bar shows no search suggestions once it is the default.

guide_caveat_context_menu.message: Chrome’s right-click item, Search [engine] for “…”, also goes through the trigger URL and opens a split view.
guide_caveat_context_menu.description: Caveat: the right-click menu item "Search X for …" also uses the trigger URL and opens the split view. Match Chrome's wording of that menu item; X stands for the search engine name.

guide_caveat_sync.message: Chrome syncs your search engine settings to all your devices, but site access doesn’t sync. Grant access on this page on each device.
guide_caveat_sync.description: Caveat: Chrome syncs search engine settings to all devices but site access granted to the extension does not sync.

guide_caveat_template_change.message: After you change an engine’s URL, copy the trigger URL again for site searches that use it on the left.
guide_caveat_template_change.description: Caveat: after changing an engine's URL, site searches that use it on the left must be copied again.

guide_caveat_remove.message: Before you delete or hide an engine, delete the Chrome site searches that use it. Otherwise, the ones with it on the left fall back to a normal search, and the ones with it on the right stop at an “Unknown engine” error page.
guide_caveat_remove.description: Caveat: delete Chrome site searches that use an engine before deleting or hiding it. "Unknown engine" refers to err_unknown_engine.

options_engines_title.description: Heading of the settings card with the engine list.

options_add_engine.description: Button that opens the dialog for adding a custom search engine.

options_engines_hint.message: Split Search needs access to the left engine’s site; for the right engine, access is recommended. To hide or delete an engine, use “Edit”; to change the order, use “Reorder”.
options_engines_hint.description: Hint under the engine list heading: site access, where Hide/Delete and the order are. The quoted button texts must match engine_edit and engine_reorder word for word. (How to write a URL template is explained in the add/edit engine dialog.)

options_hidden_title.description: Subheading above the list of hidden preset engines.

options_dlg_title_add.description: Engine dialog title when adding a new engine.

options_dlg_title_edit.description: Engine dialog title when editing an engine. The placeholder is the engine name (not translated).

options_dlg_advanced.description: Summary of the collapsed “Advanced” section in the add-engine dialog; it holds the engine id field.

options_dlg_id_label.description: Label of the engine id field in the add-engine dialog.

options_dlg_id_hint_add.message: Filled in from the name; you can change it now. Lowercase letters, digits and -, 1 to 20 characters. It goes into the trigger URL, so it can’t be changed later.
options_dlg_id_hint_add.description: Hint under the id field when adding an engine: the id is filled in from the name and can be edited; allowed characters and length; it cannot be changed later because it is written into the trigger URL.

options_dlg_id_readonly.message: ID: $ID$. It can’t be changed because it’s part of the site search URLs you saved.
options_dlg_id_readonly.description: Read-only line in the edit-engine dialog showing the engine id. $ID$ is the id.

options_dlg_id_placeholder.description: Placeholder of the id field: "e.g." plus an example id. Use the id of a search engine common in this language's market; lowercase letters, digits and - only, and it must match options_dlg_url_placeholder.

options_dlg_name_label.description: Label of the engine name field.

options_dlg_name_placeholder.description: Placeholder of the name field: "e.g." plus the name of the engine used in options_dlg_id_placeholder.

options_dlg_url_label.description: Label of the URL template field.

options_dlg_url_placeholder.description: Placeholder of the URL template field: the search URL of the engine in options_dlg_id_placeholder with %s as the query. It must be usable as the left engine: lowercase %s once, as the full value of a query parameter, no #.

options_dlg_url_hint.message: Use %s where the search terms go.
options_dlg_url_hint.description: Hint under the URL template field of the add/edit engine dialog. Keep %s as is.

options_dlg_preset_hint.message: Built-in values: $NAME$, $URL$ (change both back to restore the built-in engine)
options_dlg_preset_hint.description: Hint when editing a preset engine: shows its built-in name and URL; setting both back restores the preset.

options_dlg_edit_hint.message: If you change the URL, copy the trigger URL again for Chrome site searches that use this engine on the left.
options_dlg_edit_hint.description: Hint in the edit dialog: after changing the URL, site searches saved in Chrome that use this engine on the left must be copied again.

common_close.description: Accessible label of the close button (X icon) on a notice.

common_copy.description: Copy button next to a URL.

common_copied.description: Copy button text for 1.5 seconds after copying succeeded.

common_left.description: Small heading of the left pane (the left engine picker in settings).

common_right.description: Small heading of the right pane (the right engine picker in settings).

common_open_options.description: Button that opens the Split Search settings page (go.html error page and the toolbar popup).

common_undo.description: Button inside a notice that undoes the action just taken (e.g. hiding an engine).

notice_copy_failed.message: Couldn’t copy. Select the text and copy it yourself ($DETAIL$)
notice_copy_failed.description: Error notice when copying to the clipboard failed. The placeholder is the browser's error message.

notice_grant_failed.description: Error notice when the site access request failed. The placeholder is the error message.

notice_granted.description: Notice after the user allowed site access.

notice_grant_denied.message: Access not granted: the request was denied or the prompt was closed
notice_grant_denied.description: Warning notice when the site access prompt was denied or dismissed.

engine_list_empty.description: Shown in place of the engine list when it is empty.

engine_tag_right_only.description: Tag on an engine row: the engine can only be used on the right side.

engine_tag_default_left.description: Tag on the engine row that is the left side of the default pair.

engine_tag_default_right.description: Tag on the engine row that is the right side of the default pair.

engine_tag_no_cycle.description: Neutral tag on an engine row: this engine is unchecked in the shortcut rotation list (keyboard shortcut card).

engine_granted.description: Status on an engine row: the extension has access to the engine's site.

engine_not_granted_required.description: Status on the default left engine's row when its site is not granted; access is required.

engine_not_granted_optional.description: Status on an engine row (any engine except the default left one, including the default right one) when its site is not granted; access is only needed if the engine is used on the left.

engine_grant.description: Button on an engine row that asks Chrome for access to the engine's site.

engine_grant_named.description: Button that asks Chrome for access to the named engine's site.

engine_hide.description: Button in the edit engine dialog (built-in engines) that hides the engine.

engine_delete.description: Button in the edit engine dialog (custom engines) that deletes the engine. Also the Delete button on a custom image search engine row.

engine_delete_confirm.description: Delete button text after the first click (edit engine dialog, image search engine rows); clicking it again deletes the engine. Blur or Esc restores the button.

engine_delete_confirm_hint.message: Click again to delete “$NAME$”. Before you do, delete the Chrome site searches that use it. Otherwise, the ones with it on the left fall back to a normal search, and the ones with it on the right stop at an “Unknown engine” error page.
engine_delete_confirm_hint.description: Shown and announced inside the edit dialog, under the Delete button, when the user first clicks Delete on a custom search engine; the button now reads engine_delete_confirm. Keep the warning consistent with guide_caveat_remove.

engine_delete_confirm_again.description: Announced when the user first clicks Delete on a custom image search engine; the button now reads engine_delete_confirm.

engine_in_pair_hide.message: The default pair uses this engine, so it can’t be hidden. Choose a different engine in “Search pairs” first.
engine_in_pair_hide.description: Visible reason under the unavailable Hide button in the edit engine dialog: the default pair uses this built-in engine. The quoted tab name must match options_tab_pair exactly.

engine_in_pair_delete.message: The default pair uses this engine, so it can’t be deleted. Choose a different engine in “Search pairs” first.
engine_in_pair_delete.description: Visible reason under the unavailable Delete button in the edit engine dialog: the default pair uses this custom engine. The quoted tab name must match options_tab_pair exactly.

engine_rules_used_preset.message: Keyword rules that use this engine: $N$. While it’s hidden, they’re inactive.
engine_rules_used_preset.description: Edit-engine dialog in settings, for a preset engine (presets can only be hidden): shown when N (1 or more) keyword rules send the right side to this engine. N is the number of rules. Hiding the engine pauses those rules; they come back when the engine is restored.

engine_rules_used_custom.message: Keyword rules that use this engine: $N$. Deleting the engine deletes these rules too.
engine_rules_used_custom.description: Edit-engine dialog in settings, for a custom engine (custom engines can only be deleted): shown when N (1 or more) keyword rules send the right side to this engine. N is the number of rules. Deleting the engine deletes those rules too.

engine_edit.description: Button on an engine row that opens the edit dialog.

engine_edit_label.description: Accessible label of the Edit button on an engine row. The placeholder is the engine name. Must start with the visible text of engine_edit word for word (WCAG 2.5.3 label in name).

engine_restore.description: Button on a hidden preset engine that shows it again.

engine_left_discouraged_hint.message: Better on the right: this site handles its own page loads, so on the left you’ll usually get a normal search instead of a split view.
engine_left_discouraged_hint.description: Warning on an engine row (e.g. Perplexity): the site handles its own page loads (technically, its service worker takes over navigation), so as the left engine the split view usually doesn't open. Say it in plain words; don't mention service workers.

engine_move_up.description: Tooltip of the up-arrow icon button that moves an engine up in the list (shown only in the reorder mode).

engine_move_up_label.description: Accessible label of the up-arrow icon button (reorder mode). The placeholder is the engine name.

engine_move_down.description: Tooltip of the down-arrow icon button that moves an engine down in the list (shown only in the reorder mode).

engine_move_down_label.description: Accessible label of the down-arrow icon button (reorder mode). The placeholder is the engine name.

engine_reorder.description: Button in the engine list card header that turns on the reorder mode, where each row shows only the Move up / Move down buttons.

engine_reorder_done.description: Text of the same header button while the reorder mode is on; clicking it leaves the mode (the order is saved right away).

engine_reorder_hint.message: Use “Move up” and “Move down” on each row to change the order. Changes save automatically. The drop-down menus and the shortcut rotation use this order.
engine_reorder_hint.description: Hint under the engine list heading while the reorder mode is on; also announced to screen readers when the mode starts. The quoted button names must match engine_move_up and engine_move_down word for word.

engine_moved.description: Screen reader announcement after an engine is moved in the reorder mode (not shown on screen). $NAME$ = engine name, $POS$ = its new position (from 1), $TOTAL$ = number of visible engines. Write it so it reads correctly for any number (no plural forms).

engine_left_discouraged_suffix.description: Option text in the left engine pickers (the default pair card and the pair generator) for an engine better used on the right (e.g. Perplexity). The placeholder is the engine name.

guide_default_tag.description: Tag on the trigger URL card for the default pair.

guide_default_url_title.message: Trigger URL for the default pair
guide_default_url_title.description: Summary of the collapsible section on the Add to Chrome card that holds the default pair's trigger URL. Shown collapsed while the Get started card is on the page, since that card already shows the same URL.

guide_pair_label.description: Name of an engine pair on the trigger URL card: left engine, a separator, right engine.

guide_pair_invalid.description: Shown on the trigger URL card instead of the pair name when the default pair is invalid.

guide_no_trigger.message: Can’t create a trigger URL. Check the left engine of the default pair.
guide_no_trigger.description: Error on the trigger URL card when no trigger URL can be built for the default pair.

guide_default_hint.message: Add or update this site search in Chrome using the URL above, then choose “Make default” from its ⋮ menu. After that, searching from the address bar or dragging text to the tab strip opens a split view.
guide_default_hint.description: Instructions next to the default trigger URL: add or update the site search in Chrome with this URL and make it the default. “Make default” must match Chrome’s label; ⋮ is the More actions menu icon.

guide_other_pairs_title.description: Title of the card that generates trigger URLs for other engine pairs.

guide_pair_shortcut_hint.message: Add each pair as its own site search and start it with a shortcut you pick, for example by typing “$EXAMPLE$” in the address bar.
guide_pair_shortcut_hint.description: Hint on the other pairs card. The placeholder is guide_example_shortcut_query.

guide_example_shortcut_query.description: Example of what to type in the address bar: a shortcut for a Kagi | Bing pair, a space, then the search words (the word for "keywords" in this language).

guide_no_left.message: No engine can be used on the left.
guide_no_left.description: Shown in the pair generator when no engine can be used on the left.

guide_not_left.message: $NAME$ can’t be used as the left engine.
guide_not_left.description: Shown in the pair generator when the chosen left engine cannot be used on the left.

guide_left_not_granted.message: Split Search can’t access the left engine, $NAME$, yet, so this pair opens a normal $NAME$ search instead of a split view.
guide_left_not_granted.description: Warning in the pair generator: the left engine's site is not granted, so this pair opens a plain search instead of a split view.

guide_left_discouraged.message: $NAME$ is better on the right. Its site handles its own page loads, so on the left you usually get a normal $NAME$ search instead of a split view. On the right it isn’t affected.
guide_left_discouraged.description: Warning when an engine like Perplexity is the left side of a pair: the site handles its own page loads (technically, its service worker takes over navigation), so on the left it usually opens a plain search. Say it in plain words; don't mention service workers.

notice_action_failed.description: Fallback error notice when an action failed without a known reason.

notice_save_failed.description: Error when saving settings failed. The placeholder is the reason (another message or a browser error).

notice_save_partial.message: Saved, but a related setting couldn’t be cleared: $DETAIL$
notice_save_partial.description: Warning when the change was saved but a related setting (for example the chosen lookup or image search engine) could not be removed afterwards. The placeholder is the reason (another message or a browser error).

notice_saved.description: Notice after saving changes to an engine.

notice_needs_grant.message: Split Search doesn’t have access to its site yet. Click the highlighted “Grant access” button in its row.
notice_needs_grant.description: Sentence shown right after notice_added / notice_saved when the engine's site is not granted yet. The quoted button is engine_grant.

notice_template_changed.message: “$NAME$” has a new URL. Any site search with it on the left needs a new trigger URL. Copy the new one from “Add to Chrome” and paste it into that site search in Chrome settings.
notice_template_changed.description: Sticky notice after an engine's URL changed: site searches that use it on the left need the trigger URL copied again from the Add to Chrome tab and replaced in Chrome's settings. The quoted tab name must match options_tab_add exactly.

notice_template_changed_go.description: Button in the notice notice_template_changed; opens the Add to Chrome tab at the trigger URLs.

notice_hidden.description: Notice after hiding a preset engine.

notice_deleted.description: Notice after deleting a custom engine.

notice_deleted_with_rules.message: “$ENGINE$” deleted, along with the rules that used it ($N$)
notice_deleted_with_rules.description: Notice after deleting a custom engine that keyword rules used; those rules were deleted with it. ENGINE is the engine name, N the number of deleted rules (1 or more).

notice_restored.description: Notice after restoring a hidden preset engine.

notice_order_save_failed.description: Error when saving the engine order failed. The placeholder is the reason.

notice_load_failed.description: Error when the settings could not be read. The placeholder is the reason.

notice_pair_saved.message: Default pair saved. Copy the new URL from “Default pair” to update the matching site search in Chrome.
notice_pair_saved.description: Notice after changing the default pair once setup is done: asks the user to copy the new URL from the default pair card and update the matching site search in Chrome. Does not claim to have read Chrome’s settings. The quoted card name must match options_pair_title.

notice_pair_saved_setup.message: Default pair saved. The URL in “Get started” now uses the new pair.
notice_pair_saved_setup.description: Notice after changing the default pair during first-run setup. The quoted card name must match setup_title.

notice_pair_saved_back.description: Notice after changing the default pair back to the pair it had before on this page (nothing to update in Chrome).

setup_title.description: Heading of the first-run “Get started” card at the top of the settings page.

setup_grant_title.message: Allow access to the engine sites
setup_grant_title.description: Get started step 1 heading: grant access to the default pair's engine sites.

setup_grant_text.message: Split Search turns searches on the left engine’s site, $LEFT$, into a split view, so it needs access to that site. If you also allow the right engine, $RIGHT$, a new search updates the split view that’s already open. Access covers only these two sites.
setup_grant_text.description: Get started step 1: why access to the left (required) and right (recommended) engine sites is needed. Plain words, no talk of intercepting requests.

setup_grant_text_left.message: Split Search turns searches on the left engine’s site, $LEFT$, into a split view, so it needs access to that site. Access covers only this site.
setup_grant_text_left.description: Get started step 1 when only the left engine needs access (the right one is the same engine or already granted).

setup_grant_both.description: Get started button that requests access to both default engines' sites: left required, right recommended.

setup_grant_left.description: Get started button that requests access to the default left engine's site (required).

setup_grant_right.description: Get started button shown after the left engine is granted: requests access to the right engine's site (recommended).

setup_granted.description: Get started step 1 status once the left engine's site is granted, next to a check icon.

setup_right_hint.message: Allowing the right engine, $RIGHT$, too lets a new search update the split view that’s already open.
setup_right_hint.description: Get started step 1, after the left engine is granted: why the right engine's site is still worth granting.

setup_add_title.message: Add a site search in Chrome and make it the default
setup_add_title.description: Get started step 2 heading. "Site search" and "Make default" are Chrome's terms (see docs/i18n/chrome-terms.md).

setup_add_open.message: Copy the settings address below and paste it into the address bar.
setup_add_open.description: Get started step 2, first numbered sub-step: copy chrome://settings/searchEngines (shown below with its own Copy address button) and paste it into the address bar to open Chrome's search engine settings.

setup_add_paste.message: Next to “Site search”, click “Add”. Enter any name and shortcut, paste the trigger URL below into “URL with %s in place of query”, and click “Add”.
setup_add_paste.description: Get started step 2, second sub-step: add a site search and paste the trigger URL (shown below with its own Copy button). Field and button names must match Chrome's labels (docs/i18n/chrome-terms.md, Chrome's .pak).

setup_add_default.message: Open the new entry’s ⋮ menu and choose “Make default”.
setup_add_default.description: Get started step 2, third sub-step: make the new site search the default. “Make default” must match Chrome's label; ⋮ is the More actions menu icon.

setup_details_link.description: Link in Get started step 2 that jumps to the Add to Chrome card with the full steps.

setup_change_pair.description: Link at the end of step 2 of the “Get started” card; opens the Search pairs tab and focuses the left engine picker.

setup_try_title.message: Check that a split view opens
setup_try_title.description: Get started step 3 heading: try a search and confirm that a split view opens.

setup_try_button.description: Get started step 3 button: opens a sample search with the default pair in a new tab.

setup_try_hint.message: This searches for “$QUERY$” with your default pair. Then search for anything from the address bar. If a split view opens, you’re all set.
setup_try_hint.description: Under the Try it button: what it opens, and how to finish setup (a real search from the address bar). The placeholder is setup_sample_query.

setup_try_blocked.description: Inline reason next to the disabled Try it button: the left engine's site is not granted yet.

setup_sample_query.description: Sample search words the Try it button searches for. Pick a short, natural everyday search in this language (not about this extension).

setup_done_title.description: Get started card after setup is detected as complete (shown once, on the page that saw it).

setup_done_text.message: Searching from the address bar or dragging text to the tab strip opens a split view.

setup_done_notice.message: Setup complete. Searching from the address bar or dragging text to the tab strip opens a split view.
setup_done_notice.description: Notice announced when setup is detected as complete.

setup_regrant_title.description: Get started card heading when setup was done before but the left engine's site is not granted now.

setup_regrant_text.message: Split Search can’t access the left engine, $LEFT$. For now, searches open a normal $LEFT$ search.
setup_regrant_text.description: Get started card when setup was done before but the left engine's site is not granted now: searches fall back to a plain search.

setup_revoked_notice.message: Access to the left engine, $LEFT$, was removed. Searches now open a normal $LEFT$ search.
setup_revoked_notice.description: Notice when access to the default left engine's site is removed while the settings page is open.

options_left_not_granted.message: Split Search can’t access the left engine, $NAME$, yet. For now, searches open a normal $NAME$ search instead of a split view.
options_left_not_granted.description: Warning in the default pair card: the left engine's site is not granted, so searches open a plain search instead of a split view.

lang_label.description: Label of the language drop-down at the top of the settings page.

lang_auto.description: First option of the language drop-down: use the browser's language. The placeholder is the native name of the language the browser currently resolves to (one of the lang_name_* messages).

lang_note.message: The toolbar button tooltip and the extension description on chrome://extensions and the Chrome Web Store always follow the browser language. This setting doesn’t change them.
lang_note.description: Note under the language drop-down: the extension description, the toolbar button tooltip, the description on chrome://extensions and the Chrome Web Store listing always follow the browser language, not this choice. Keep chrome://extensions as is.

lang_name_en.description: Native name of English in the language drop-down (本名，不要翻译): identical in every locale, do not translate.

lang_name_zh_cn.description: Native name of Simplified Chinese in the language drop-down (本名，不要翻译): identical in every locale, do not translate.

lang_name_zh_tw.description: Native name of Traditional Chinese in the language drop-down (本名，不要翻译): identical in every locale, do not translate.

lang_name_es.description: Native name of Spanish in the language drop-down (本名，不要翻译): identical in every locale, do not translate.

options_narrow_label.message: Open the right side in a background tab when the window is narrow
options_narrow_label.description: Name of the switch in the default pair card. Narrow means the window is under 960 px wide.

options_narrow_hint.message: Below 960 px wide, a split view gets too cramped. With this on, the left results stay in the tab you searched from, and the right results open in the tab next to it.
options_narrow_hint.description: Hint under the narrow-window switch on the settings page, describing what happens when it is on. Split view is Chrome's feature name; keep the Chrome term. Do not say "this tab": the reader is on the settings page.

options_rules_title.message: Keyword rules for the right side
options_rules_title.description: Settings, Search pairs tab: heading of the keyword rules card (rules that switch the default pair's right engine when the search contains certain words or a writing system).

options_rules_intro.message: When a search matches a rule, the default pair’s right side switches to that rule’s engine. The left side stays the same. Rules are checked from top to bottom, and the first match wins. Rules don’t apply to searches made with another pair’s trigger URL.
options_rules_intro.description: Keyword rules card: what the rules do. The last sentence says searches made with the trigger URL of a pair other than the default pair don't use the rules.

options_rules_privacy.message: Matching happens on this device, and your searches aren’t sent anywhere else. You write the words in your rules yourself, and they sync with Chrome like your other settings.
options_rules_privacy.description: Keyword rules card: privacy note. Matching runs locally; the rules sync with the user's other settings through Chrome sync.

options_rules_empty.message: No rules yet. The right side always uses the default pair’s right engine.
options_rules_empty.description: Keyword rules card: shown when there are no rules.

options_rules_words_row.description: Keyword rules list: start of a row for a word rule. WORDS is the rule's words joined with options_rules_word_sep. The row continues with a space and one of the options_rules_target* texts.

options_rules_script_row.description: Keyword rules list: start of a row for a writing-system rule. SCRIPT is the writing-system name (script_han, script_kana, script_hangul or script_cyrillic). The row continues with a space and one of the options_rules_target* texts.

options_rules_word_sep.description: Keyword rules list: separator between the words of one rule (inserted into options_rules_words_row). Include any space the language needs after it.

options_rules_target.description: Keyword rules list: end of a row, the engine the rule puts on the right side. ENGINE is the engine name (or the text of popup_engine_deleted).

options_rules_target_default.message: → $ENGINE$ (same as the default pair’s right side)
options_rules_target_default.description: Keyword rules list: end of a row whose engine happens to be the default pair's current right engine. ENGINE is that engine's name.

options_rules_target_keep.description: Keyword rules list: end of a row for an exception rule, which keeps the default pair's right engine (and follows it if the default pair changes). ENGINE is the current right engine's name.

options_rules_off_hidden.description: Keyword rules list: shown under a rule that is paused because its engine is hidden. It works again once the engine is restored. ENGINE is the engine name.

options_rules_off_missing.message: Inactive: the right-side engine was deleted
options_rules_off_missing.description: Keyword rules list: shown under a rule that is paused because its engine no longer exists (deleted, or synced from another device without that engine).

options_rules_off_left.message: Inactive: $ENGINE$ is the default pair’s left engine
options_rules_off_left.description: Keyword rules list: shown under a rule that is paused because its engine is now the default pair's left engine. ENGINE is the engine name.

options_rules_shadowed.message: “$WORD$” is already caught by rule $N$, so it never matches here
options_rules_shadowed.description: Keyword rules list: shown under a rule when one of its words can never match, because an earlier rule already matches every search that has it. WORD is that word; N is the earlier rule's position, counting from 1.

options_rules_shadowed_rule.message: Rule $N$ already covers this one, so this rule never matches
options_rules_shadowed_rule.description: Keyword rules list: shown under a writing-system rule that can never match, because an earlier rule checks the same writing system. N is the earlier rule's position, counting from 1.

options_rules_add.description: Keyword rules card: button that opens the dialog to add a rule.

options_rules_edit.description: Keyword rules list: button on each row that opens the rule dialog.

options_rules_edit_aria.description: Accessible name of options_rules_edit. Must start with the visible text of options_rules_edit. Position of the rule in the list, counting from 1.

options_rules_up.description: Keyword rules list: button that moves the rule up one position.

options_rules_up_aria.description: Accessible name of options_rules_up. Must start with the visible text of options_rules_up. Position of the rule in the list, counting from 1.

options_rules_down.description: Keyword rules list: button that moves the rule down one position.

options_rules_down_aria.description: Accessible name of options_rules_down. Must start with the visible text of options_rules_down. Position of the rule in the list, counting from 1.

options_rules_delete.description: Rule dialog (edit mode only): button that deletes the rule. Needs a second click to confirm.

options_rules_delete_confirm.description: Rule dialog: text of the delete button after the first click; clicking again deletes the rule.

options_rules_delete_hint.message: Click again to delete this rule.
options_rules_delete_hint.description: Rule dialog: status line shown (and read by screen readers) after the first click on the delete button.

options_rules_dialog_add.description: Title of the rule dialog when adding a rule.

options_rules_dialog_edit.description: Title of the rule dialog when editing a rule.

options_rules_when_legend.message: When to switch the right side
options_rules_when_legend.description: Rule dialog: label of the group of two radio buttons that choose the rule's condition.

options_rules_when_words.description: Rule dialog: radio button, the rule matches when the search contains one of the listed words.

options_rules_when_script.message: The search uses a writing system
options_rules_when_script.description: Rule dialog: radio button, the rule matches when the search contains at least one character of a chosen writing system.

options_rules_words_label.description: Rule dialog: label of the words field.

options_rules_words_hint.message: Separate words with commas, for example: weather, forecast. Case and full-width or half-width forms don’t matter. English words match only as whole words, so js doesn’t match jsonl.
options_rules_words_hint.description: Rule dialog: hint under the words field. The example words are typed by the user, so they may be translated; keep the js/jsonl example as is.

options_rules_strip_label.message: Remove these words from the search
options_rules_strip_label.description: Rule dialog: checkbox label under the words field.

options_rules_strip_hint.message: For example, with the word vd, “vd cats” becomes just “cats” on both sides. If the search is only these words, nothing is removed.
options_rules_strip_hint.description: Rule dialog: hint under the strip checkbox.

options_discard_title.description: Confirm dialog shown when clicking outside a settings dialog with unsaved edits: title.

options_discard_drop.description: Confirm dialog: button that closes the form and drops the edits.

options_discard_keep.description: Confirm dialog: button that returns to the form to keep editing.

options_rules_strip_row.description: Rule row: note after the target engine when the rule removes its words from the search. Keep the leading middle dot; the row reads like “Contains vd → YouTube · removes these words”.

options_rules_script_label.description: Rule dialog: label of the writing-system dropdown (options are script_option_han, script_option_kana, script_option_hangul, script_option_cyrillic). Use the same word as err_rule_script.

options_rules_script_hint.message: One such character is enough, so almost every Chinese search matches. Japanese searches often include Chinese characters, so put “Japanese kana” above “Chinese characters”.
options_rules_script_hint.description: Rule dialog: hint under the writing-system dropdown. Use the same names as script_option_kana and script_option_han.

options_rules_engine_label.description: Rule dialog: label of the dropdown that chooses the engine for the right side.

options_rules_engine_keep.message: The default pair’s right side (no change)
options_rules_engine_keep.description: Rule dialog, engine dropdown: option that makes the rule an exception and keeps the default pair's right engine (it follows the default pair if that changes).

options_rules_engine_pick.description: Rule dialog, engine dropdown: empty placeholder option shown until the user chooses an engine.

options_rules_engine_hidden.description: Rule dialog, engine dropdown: extra option for the rule's current engine when that engine is hidden (only while editing that rule). ENGINE is the engine name.

notice_narrow_saved.description: Notice after toggling the narrow-window checkbox.

catalog_cat_translate.description: Category heading in the engine catalog dialog: Translation.

catalog_cat_reference.description: Category heading in the engine catalog dialog: Reference.

catalog_cat_video.description: Category heading in the engine catalog dialog: Video.

catalog_cat_dev.description: Category heading in the engine catalog dialog: Development.

catalog_cat_maps.description: Category heading in the engine catalog dialog: Maps.

catalog_cat_academic.description: Category heading in the engine catalog dialog: Academic.

catalog_cat_shopping.description: Category heading in the engine catalog dialog: Shopping.

catalog_cat_ai.description: Catalog category heading: AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude). The prompt is prefilled, not sent.

err_catalog_already_added.message: “$NAME$” is already in your engine list.
err_catalog_already_added.description: Error when adding a catalog engine that already exists. $NAME$ is the engine name.

err_not_results_page.message: This page has changed. Click the toolbar button again.
err_not_results_page.description: Toolbar popup, completing a split view: the page is no longer a recognized search results page (navigated away, closed, joined a split view or the query is gone) when the user clicked an engine.

err_window_unsupported.message: Split view isn’t available in this window.
err_window_unsupported.description: Toolbar popup, completing a split view: the current window can't hold a split view (for example a popup or picture-in-picture window).

err_split_failed.message: Couldn’t open the search on the right. Try again.
err_split_failed.description: Toolbar popup, completing a split view: opening the right-side search failed.

err_message_rejected.message: That didn’t work. Click the toolbar button and try again.
err_message_rejected.description: Toolbar popup, completing a split view: the extension rejected the request (unknown sender, bad fields, or the chosen engine is no longer available).

err_rule_no_words.description: Keyword rule dialog, words field: the user entered no words.

err_rule_too_many_words.message: A rule can have up to 30 words
err_rule_too_many_words.description: Keyword rule dialog, words field: one rule has more than 30 words.

err_rule_words_total.message: All rules together can have up to 60 words
err_rule_words_total.description: Keyword rule dialog, words field: all rules together would have more than 60 words.

err_rule_word_long.message: “$WORD$…” is too long. Each word can be up to 32 characters.
err_rule_word_long.description: Keyword rule dialog, words field: one word is longer than 32 characters (code points, after normalization). $WORD$ is the first 12 characters of that word; the word is always longer, so the message adds the ellipsis after $WORD$.

err_rule_too_many.message: You can have up to 20 rules
err_rule_too_many.description: Keyword rules: the user tried to add a 21st rule (the limit is 20).

err_rule_script.description: Keyword rule dialog: the rule is 'the search contains a writing system' (Han characters, Japanese kana, Hangul, Cyrillic) but none was chosen.

err_rule_engine.message: Choose an engine for the right side
err_rule_engine.description: Keyword rule dialog: no valid engine was chosen for the right side (none chosen, hidden, or it is now the default left engine).

err_rule_too_large.message: These rules are too long to save. Remove some words, then save again.
err_rule_too_large.description: Keyword rule dialog: all rules together would be too large to store in Chrome sync (over 8000 bytes).

err_rule_gone.message: This rule was already deleted elsewhere
err_rule_gone.description: Keyword rules: the rule being saved or moved was already deleted on another settings page or synced device.

options_add_from_catalog.description: Button next to 'Add engine' that opens the engine catalog dialog.

catalog_title.description: Title of the engine catalog dialog.

catalog_hint.message: These sites work well on the right side of a split view. Once added, they work like any other custom engine: you can edit or delete them.
catalog_hint.description: Short intro in the engine catalog dialog. Custom engine = user-defined search engine entry.

catalog_add.description: Button on a catalog row that adds the engine.

catalog_added.description: Disabled button on a catalog row whose engine is already in the list.

catalog_add_aria.description: Accessible name of the Add button on a catalog row. The placeholder is the engine name. Must contain the visible text of catalog_add word for word (WCAG 2.5.3 label in name).

catalog_added_aria.description: Accessible name of the disabled Added button on a catalog row. The placeholder is the engine name. Must contain the visible text of catalog_added word for word (WCAG 2.5.3 label in name).

notice_catalog_added.description: Notice after adding an engine from the catalog. $NAME$ is the engine name.

cmd_cycle_right.message: Switch the right side to the next engine
cmd_cycle_right.description: Description of the keyboard command, shown on chrome://extensions/shortcuts. The command switches the right side of a Split Search split view to the next engine in the rotation.

options_shortcut_title.description: Heading of the keyboard shortcut card on the settings page.

options_shortcut_hint.message: In a split view opened by Split Search, press the shortcut to switch the right side to the next engine in the rotation (choose them below). No shortcut is set by default. Click “Set shortcut” to choose one on Chrome’s Keyboard shortcuts page.
options_shortcut_hint.description: Hint in the keyboard shortcut card; the rotation checkboxes are below it in the same card. The page name must match Chrome's own title of chrome://extensions/shortcuts (Keyboard shortcuts); the quoted button text must match options_shortcut_open.

options_shortcut_label.description: Label before the current key combination (or the not-set text) in the keyboard shortcut card.

options_shortcut_unset.description: Shown instead of a key combination when the user has not bound the command. Use Chrome's own wording for an unbound shortcut (Not set).

options_shortcut_open.description: Button that opens chrome://extensions/shortcuts, where the user binds the key combination.

options_cycle_title.description: Collapsible summary in the keyboard shortcut card above the rotation checkboxes. $ON$ = engines included in the rotation, $ALL$ = visible engines. Write it so it reads correctly for any number (no plural forms).

options_cycle_hint.message: Engines rotate in the order of the engine list, skipping unchecked engines and the current left engine.
options_cycle_hint.description: Legend of the rotation checkbox group in the keyboard shortcut card: the order of rotation and what is skipped.

popup_not_ours.message: This tab isn’t in a split view opened by Split Search.
popup_not_ours.description: Explains that the toolbar popup has nothing to switch: the current tab is not in a split view that Split Search opened. "Split view" must match Chrome's term. Keep Split Search untranslated.

popup_idle_hint.message: Try searching from the address bar, or drag text to the tab strip.
popup_idle_hint.description: Popup, under popup_not_ours: what to try to open a split view.

popup_setup_needed.message: Setup isn’t finished, so searches won’t open a split view yet.
popup_setup_needed.description: Toolbar popup, outside a Split Search split view, when the default pair's left engine is not granted: searching only does a plain search. Shown with the popup_setup_button primary button.

popup_setup_regrant.message: Split Search can’t access $NAME$ anymore, so searches won’t open a split view for now.
popup_setup_regrant.description: Toolbar popup, outside a Split Search split view, when setup was finished before but the default pair's left engine ($NAME$, an engine name) is no longer granted: searches only do a plain search. Replaces popup_setup_needed; shown with the popup_setup_button primary button.

popup_setup_button.description: Toolbar popup primary button: opens the settings page at the Get started card.

popup_setup_try_note.message: If a search doesn’t open a split view, finish step 2 in settings.
popup_setup_try_note.description: Toolbar popup, under popup_idle_hint, when the left engine is granted but setup isn't confirmed yet (also for users upgraded from an older version who already set things up): a conditional hint, must not say setup is unfinished. Step 2 = adding the site search in the Get started card. Followed by the popup_setup_link button.

popup_setup_link.description: Toolbar popup text button after popup_setup_try_note: opens the settings page at the Get started card.

popup_shortcut_label.description: Popup footer, before the key combination of the shortcut that switches the right side to the next engine.

popup_query_label.description: Toolbar popup: label in front of the search terms of the current split view.

popup_lookup_label.description: Toolbar popup, lookup pair (the user's web page next to a lookup result opened from the right-click menu): label in front of what is being looked up: the selected text, or "Image: <host>" for an image. Used instead of "Search terms" because an image lookup has no search terms.

popup_empty_query.description: Toolbar popup: shown instead of the search terms when the search was empty.

popup_left_label.description: Toolbar popup: label in front of the engine shown on the left side of the split view.

popup_right_label.description: Toolbar popup: label in front of the engine shown on the right side of the split view.

popup_engine_deleted.description: Toolbar popup: shown instead of an engine name when that engine has since been deleted in settings.

popup_role_page.description: Toolbar popup, lookup pair (the user's web page next to a lookup result opened from the right-click menu): label in front of the user's own page. Used instead of "Left" because the user may have swapped the two sides.

popup_role_lookup.description: Toolbar popup, lookup pair: label in front of the engine showing the lookup result (the side the engine list switches). Used instead of "Right" because the user may have swapped the two sides.

popup_page_origin.description: Toolbar popup, lookup pair: shown as the "engine name" of the user's own page side. Do not say "current page": the popup may be opened from the lookup side.

popup_lookup_image.description: Toolbar popup, image lookup pair: shown instead of the search terms. The placeholder is the host of the image URL (for example img.example.com); the image itself is not loaded.

popup_switch_title.description: Toolbar popup: heading above the list of engines; clicking one loads it on the right side.

popup_lookup_switch_title.description: Toolbar popup, lookup pair: heading above the list of engines; clicking one loads it on the lookup side. Used instead of "Switch the right side to" because the user may have swapped the two sides.

popup_no_choices.message: No other engines to switch to.
popup_no_choices.description: Toolbar popup: shown instead of the engine list when there is no other engine to switch to.

popup_switch_failed.description: Toolbar popup: shown when switching to the clicked engine failed (the split view was closed or split up, or loading the engine failed). Doesn't say "right side": in a lookup pair the switched side may be on the left.

popup_rule_word.message: Your search has “$WORD$”, so the right side switched to $ENGINE$.
popup_rule_word.description: Toolbar popup, own search pair: shown under the left/right panes when a keyword rule replaced the default pair's right engine because the search contains one of the rule's words. WORD is the matched word from the user's own rule; ENGINE is the current right-side engine name.

popup_rule_script.message: Your search has $SCRIPT$, so the right side switched to $ENGINE$.
popup_rule_script.description: Toolbar popup, own search pair: shown when a keyword rule replaced the default pair's right engine because the search contains a writing system. SCRIPT is the writing-system name (script_han, script_kana, script_hangul or script_cyrillic); ENGINE is the current right-side engine name.

popup_rule_generic.message: A keyword rule chose the right side.
popup_rule_generic.description: Toolbar popup, own search pair: shown when a keyword rule picked the right-side engine but the rule has since been changed or deleted, so the popup cannot say which word matched.

popup_rule_revert.description: Toolbar popup: button next to the keyword-rule note; switches the right side back to the default pair's right engine. ENGINE is that engine's name.

script_han.description: Writing-system name (Han characters, used in Chinese and in Japanese kanji). Shown mid-sentence inside popup_rule_script and options_rules_script_row, so keep the casing a sentence needs (the dialog option uses script_option_*).

script_kana.description: Writing-system name (Japanese hiragana and katakana). Shown mid-sentence inside popup_rule_script and options_rules_script_row, so keep the casing a sentence needs (the dialog option uses script_option_*).

script_hangul.description: Writing-system name (Korean Hangul). Shown mid-sentence inside popup_rule_script and options_rules_script_row, so keep the casing a sentence needs (the dialog option uses script_option_*).

script_cyrillic.description: Writing-system name (Cyrillic letters, used in Russian, Ukrainian and others). Shown mid-sentence inside popup_rule_script and options_rules_script_row, so keep the casing a sentence needs (the dialog option uses script_option_*).

script_option_han.description: Option in the writing-system dropdown of the keyword-rule dialog in settings (Han characters, used in Chinese and in Japanese kanji). Stands alone, so capitalize it as a list item; same name as script_han.

script_option_kana.description: Option in the writing-system dropdown of the keyword-rule dialog in settings (Japanese kana). Stands alone, so capitalize it as a list item; same name as script_kana.

script_option_hangul.description: Option in the writing-system dropdown of the keyword-rule dialog in settings (Korean Hangul). Stands alone, so capitalize it as a list item; same name as script_hangul.

script_option_cyrillic.description: Option in the writing-system dropdown of the keyword-rule dialog in settings (Cyrillic letters, used in Russian, Ukrainian and others). Stands alone, so capitalize it as a list item; same name as script_cyrillic.

popup_complete_detected.description: Toolbar popup, completing a split view: shown when the current tab is a search results page of a configured engine. $ENGINE$ is the engine name, $QUERY$ the recognized search terms.

popup_complete_hint.message: Pick an engine for the right side
popup_complete_hint.description: Toolbar popup, completing a split view: heading above the engine buttons. Clicking one keeps the current page on the left and opens the same search with that engine on the right.

popup_complete_aria.description: Toolbar popup, completing a split view: accessible name of an engine button. Must start with the engine name, which is the button's visible text.

popup_complete_narrow.message: The window is narrow, so the right side opened in the next tab.
popup_complete_narrow.description: Toolbar popup, completing a split view: shown after the click when the window is narrow, so the right-side search opened in the background tab next to the current one instead of a split view.

popup_complete_plain.message: Couldn’t make a split view. The search opened in the next tab.
popup_complete_plain.description: Toolbar popup, completing a split view: shown after the click when Chrome couldn't put the two tabs into a split view; the right-side search opened in the tab next to the current one.

options_lookup_title.description: Title of the settings card for the right-click lookup feature (select text or right-click an image).

options_lookup_intro.message: Select text on a web page and right-click it, or right-click an image, then choose the Split Search item. The page stays on the left and the result opens on the right.
options_lookup_intro.description: Intro of the right-click lookup card. Menu items are added by Split Search to Chrome's right-click menu.

options_lookup_engine_label.description: Label of the dropdown that picks the engine used to look up selected text.

options_lookup_follow.message: Same as the right side of the default pair (now: $ENGINE$)
options_lookup_follow.description: First option of the text lookup dropdown: use whatever engine is on the right side of the default pair. $ENGINE$ is its current name.

options_image_engine_label.description: Label of the dropdown that picks the reverse image search engine.

options_image_list_title.description: Heading above the list of reverse image search engines.

options_image_add_catalog.description: Button that opens the catalog of reverse image search engines.

options_image_add_custom.description: Button that opens the dialog for adding a custom reverse image search engine.

options_image_note_embedded.message: Images embedded in the page have no public address, so they can’t be searched. The menu item doesn’t appear for them.
options_image_note_embedded.description: Limitation note: images that exist only inside a page (no public URL).

options_image_note_login.message: If you have to sign in to see an image, the engine usually can’t get it.
options_image_note_login.description: Limitation note: images that need a login.

options_lookup_privacy.message: Selected text and image addresses go only to the engines you choose here. Some image addresses include access credentials, so the engine can open that image too. An image address may also show which site it came from.
options_lookup_privacy.description: Privacy note: what is sent to the chosen engine.

options_lookup_notes_title.description: Summary of the collapsed notes block in the right-click lookup card (privacy note and image limitations).

catalog_image_title.description: Title of the dialog listing ready-made reverse image search engines.

catalog_image_hint.message: Once added, they work like any custom image search engine: you can pick or delete them.
catalog_image_hint.description: Short intro in the image search catalog dialog.

options_image_dlg_title.description: Title of the dialog for adding a custom image search engine.

options_image_url_placeholder.description: Placeholder of the address template field of an image search engine (example address with %s).

options_image_dlg_hint.message: Use %s where the image address goes.
options_image_dlg_hint.description: Hint under the address template field of an image search engine. Keep %s as is.

notice_lookup_saved.description: Notice after choosing the text lookup engine.

notice_image_engine_saved.description: Notice after choosing the image search engine.

notice_rule_saved.description: Notice after adding or editing a keyword rule in settings.

notice_rule_deleted.description: Notice after deleting a keyword rule in settings.

notice_rule_moved.description: Notice (read by screen readers) after moving a keyword rule up or down. N is the rule's new position, counting from 1.

menu_lookup_text.description: Right-click menu item shown when text is selected on a web page: the page stays on the left and the text lookup engine opens on the right. $ENGINE$ is the engine name. Keep %s as is: Chrome replaces it with the selected text.

menu_lookup_image.message: Search image with $ENGINE$ in split view
menu_lookup_image.description: Right-click menu item shown on an image on a web page: the page stays on the left and the image search engine opens on the right. $ENGINE$ is the engine name.
